items.title: Amazon Connect Customer lets agents pause and resume emails
items.content_snippet: Amazon Connect Customer lets agents pause emails while waiting for information or approvals, freeing them to handle higher-priority contacts and resume their work later. For example, an agent waiting for a supervisor to approve a refund can pause the email and take an incoming call. Paused time is tracked separately from active handling time, giving supervisors a more accurate view of the time agents spend working on emails. items.title: Qodo brings company context into Codex code review
items.content_snippet: Qodo’s Codex plugin brings company context, codebase standards, and independent review into the development workflow. It helps developers catch bugs across repositories, where a change can look right in one codebase and break a service in another. In Behind the Build, co-founder Itamar Friedman and AI DevRel lead Nnenna Ndukwe discuss how they’re building with GPT-6 Astra and their vision for a workflow where one agent writes code and another challenges it. Read the full story: https://openai.co

Learn more about OpenAI Private Intelligence: https://openai.com/business/private-intelligence/

items.title: Don't Approve the AI Model. Approve the App - Doneyli De Jesus, Langfuse
items.content_snippet: Doneyli De Jesus, who leads AI engineering solutions at Langfuse by ClickHouse, shares how his team helped a top-five bank put deployment gates on AI agents. Banks don't certify models, they certify applications, and they need setups that are on-premises, gated and air-gapped. He walks through building a golden data set, scoring traces across several dimensions, and how a small model that was 97% grounded but only 60% accurate on numbers cleared the bank's 85% gate once it got a calculator tool.

items.title: Why Datasite Stopped Building Its Own Parsing - Adit Abraham, Reducto & Raj Bakhru, Datasite
items.content_snippet: Datasite global CTO Raj Bakhru talks with Reducto co-founder and CEO Adit Abraham about leading AI at a platform that handles about 60% of deals over $100 million. Raj shares how his startup BlueFlame was acquired into Datasite, why parsing billions of pages of deal documents is "all edge cases," and how he decides what his 250 engineers build versus buy. He also covers how AI coding is changing who he hires, and VDR Bench, the internal eval where better parsing raised recall 22%. Chapters: 0:00

items.title: Building the AI Agent Is Easy. Proving It's Safe Isn't - Jonathan Osborne, NatWest
items.content_snippet: NatWest lead AI engineer Jonathan Osborne shares how the UK's second-largest retail bank, with 19 million customers and about 100,000 assistant conversations a day, is moving its digital assistant Cora from scripted answers to AI agents. Building the agent was the easy part; proving it was safe was the hard part. items.title: Why AI Makes You 100x Faster but Not Your Company - Mitchell Troyanovsky, Basis
items.content_snippet: Individual engineers have seen huge productivity gains from AI, but most companies haven't. Mitchell Troyanovsky, co-founder of Basis, argues that agents need to be simple and reliable to spread through a company, and the way to get there is to make them opinionated. items.title: Without Caching, Your AI Agent Costs 10x More - George Cameron, Artificial Analysis
items.content_snippet: Some models now cost dollars to complete a single task, while others cost a few cents. George Cameron, co-founder of Artificial Analysis, breaks down what actually drives agent costs in 2026: input tokens, cache hit rate and the number of steps. In one example, an agent task costs about $21 with caching and over $200 without it.
